title.label: Great concept but can’t get recurring alarm to work

content.label:
Love the idea! Got the app because there’s a single daily task that I want to be continuously nudged to do so I don’t forget. 

However, after setting up a recurring task and completing the task on the first day, it didn’t alert me on second day. 

I logged in and see the task had a zzzz indicator next to it.

I emailed support and sent logs and never heard back. 

It may be user error, but it’s hard to troubleshoot since the shortest duration for a recurring task is one day… so I have to fiddle with settings and wait for the following day to see if it worked!

Love that I can schedule things way in advance when I think of them. What a great tool! I use this most days.

As a suggestion, I wish I could customize the theme to be more personalized with colors or background images. Additionally, maybe consider setting up groupings for the logged items as opposed to one massive list, by date or month. Maybe a fun stats page with keywords for most common logged tasks.

title.label: A great app with greater potential!

content.label: Love this app! It’s helped a lot with my accountability. With everything I tried before, if I couldn’t do it the second the alarm or reminder went off, I’d immediately forget it. The persistent reminders help immensely. I’d rate 5 but there’s room to grow. Timers are kind of limited. I’d like to be able to associate a timer with a task. So so long as that timer is running, it won’t ding. Think about a task called laundry. You don’t need to make and then snooze 3, you just have a snooze timer while it washes and another while it dries. A snooze all option timer would be nice too! Another feature I’d like to see is task steps. Like steps for washing drying and folding laundry but the dry step won’t go off until wash is marked done. All in all, it’s a great app with a lot of potential and well worth the price!

Love the app on the iPhone but incredibly annoying to use with Apple Watch. If you have stacked reminders (say 5 reminders at 9 AM), the expected behavior is for Apple Watch to buzz you once and say “5 notifications on Due.” It doesn’t. It buzzes you, 5 separate times. Even more annoying is that the app waits about 5-10 seconds between each buzz, so 5 notifications mean you get buzzed every 5-10 seconds for nearly a minute at every reminder or snooze period. I’ve contacted Due support who suggested some setting changes to minimize this behavior, but ultimately said, “it’s Apple’s system, we can’t do anything about it.” 

I had 14-25 notifications throughout the day. This means none stop buzzing all day. You can’t stop it either. You can’t push a button to stop. Even taking the watch off your wrist, it will continue through the notification cycle and you just have to wait if you don’t want to be buzzed constantly. 

Some days, it uses stacked notifications while other days, for no apparent reason, the app will bother you to death. 

If you’re an Apple Watch user, try a different app.

title.label: If I could give it 10 stars, I would

content.label:
I’ve had DUE for longer than I can remember, and I’ve always loved it. It’s simple, it’s easy, and—unlike so many other apps—it doesn’t cost a small fortune. It’s an affordable annual purchase (not an endless subscription), and it does exactly what it promises, in the cleanest and most straightforward way possible.
I never write app reviews because the best apps tend to fade into the background—you use them, rely on them, and stop thinking about them. But this app deserves recognition.
Earlier this year, I was diagnosed with ADHD, and everything suddenly clicked. I realized that DUE has always worked so well for me because of how frictionless it is. When something pops into my head that I need to remember, I can instantly throw it into DUE. No complexity. No setup. No mental overhead.
What truly sets this app apart is the reminder system. I don’t use calendars, task lists, or to‑do apps anymore because things get buried, endlessly snoozed, or turned into meaningless deadlines. DUE is different. If you don’t check something off, it just keeps reminding you—gently but persistently—without you having to manage or reset anything. That “nagging” feature works quietly in the background, doing exactly what it’s supposed to do. It’s simple, effective, and honestly kind of genius.
Now, DUE is where everything goes—anything I need to remember, no matter how big or small. And the funny thing is, I appreciate this app more now than I ever did when I downloaded it over five years ago. It continues to improve, continues to get better, and I genuinely don’t know what I would do without it.
Huge appreciation to the people behind this app for keeping it affordable, simple, and incredibly effective. This is the first app review I’ve ever submitted—and it’s long overdue.

I’ve written less than five reviews in over 10 years of owning iPhones. I have severe ADHD and I’ve tried most if not all of the available reminder apps. And for the reoccurring reminders, it’s nice to have the option to repeat the reminder from the date due (e.g., Take out trash every Monday) or from the completion date (e.g., Water plants 7 days after completing the reminder).
